property_summary: For any owner-funded contract balance, calling withdrawAll transfers the contract's entire ETH balance to the owner (reference preserves full-balance forwarding; the mutant that calls withdraw(0) breaks this by leaving balance in the contract for some balances).

For any initial contract balance funded by any address and any owner (the deployer), calling withdrawAll transfers the contract's entire ETH balance to the owner (reference preserves this invariant; the mutant calling withdraw(0) leaves non-zero balance in the contract for some inputs).

For any nonzero contract balance funded before withdrawAll is called by the owner, withdrawAll empties the contract (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave a nonzero balance, breaking this rule for some inputs.

For any caller who is the contract owner and any initial contract balance >= 0, calling withdrawAll causes the owner to receive exactly the contract's entire balance (so address(c).balance == 0 afterwards); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave a nonzero balance, violating this.

For any owner caller and any nonzero initial contract balance sent via a fuzzed depositor, calling withdrawAll by the owner always reduces the contract balance (address(c).balance) to strictly less than it was before the call in the reference; the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave the balance unchanged, breaking this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any contract balance, only the owner can withdraw the contract's entire balance via withdrawAll (so address(c).balance remains unchanged when a non-owner calls withdrawAll); the mutant removing onlyOwner allows some non-owner caller to drain funds, violating this.

For any caller and any starting contract balance, if the caller is not the owner then calling withdrawAll must NOT transfer funds out (address(c).balance remains the same); the mutant that removes onlyOwner allows some non-owner caller to reduce address(c).balance, violating this.

For any caller and any initial contract balance, if the caller is not the owner then calling withdrawAll reverts (or otherwise does not succeed), so the post-call owner remains the same and the contract balance is not transferred to the caller; the mutant removing onlyOwner from withdrawAll allows a non-owner caller to successfully withdraw the full balance, violating that property.

For any caller address and any nonzero contract balance funded via fallback, calling withdrawAll can only change address(c).balance if the caller is the owner; the reference enforces this by onlyOwner, while the mutant (which removes onlyOwner) allows some non-owner caller to reduce address(c).balance by draining funds.

For any attacker contract A and any nonzero initial balance funded into C by A calling C (so msg.sender when funding is A), after A (not the original deployer owner) invokes withdrawAll, the reference C preserves that the owner address remains the original deployer (owner unchanged) and the contract balance is NOT transferred to A (address(c).balance remains the same); the mutant that removed onlyOwner from withdrawAll allows a malicious caller contract A to successfully withdraw all funds to itself, changing address(c).balance and making the postcondition false.

After funding C and then calling withdrawAll as owner, the call must revert-free and preserve that address(this) of C has zero balance afterwards (i.e., withdrawAll succeeds and leaves C.balance == 0).
A withdraw(uint) call made by the owner with amount not exceeding the contract's balance should not revert.
When the caller is the contract owner, calling withdraw(uint) must not revert for any uint value (i.e., owner withdrawals never revert).
When the caller is the contract owner, calling withdraw(uint) never reverts for any uint value (i.e., owner withdraw calls always succeed).
When called by the contract owner, calling withdraw(uint) must not revert (owner withdraws never revert).

When the owner withdraws the contract balance to their address, the call must not revert (withdraw succeeds) while preserving that address(c).balance decreases by the withdrawn amount and address(c.owner) increases accordingly.

For any target and value, the reference contract C never prevents the owner from later withdrawing the contract's full balance (address(c).balance) after calling sendMoney(target, value, data) — i.e., sendMoney never reverts away the ability to withdraw the current contract balance — whereas the mutant that replaces transfer with call and requires success can revert when the callee fails, breaking this rule for some inputs (failing callee and nonzero value).
